**Question:** When an input line ends with a Windows-style carriage-return + newline (or a bare carriage return), should those exact characters be reproduced in the output, or may they be converted to a plain newline? (FR-006, FR-007, SC-003)

**Why it matters:** Logs collected from Windows hosts and many Java/.NET services use CRLF endings. If the tool quietly rewrites them, the output is no longer byte-identical to the input — which breaks the promise in SC-003 and could flag a diff for a reviewer comparing the redacted log against the original.

**Recommended:** Option A — The tool's core promise is "everything else is output unchanged." Preserving the bytes exactly keeps that promise unconditionally, costs nothing to implement, and avoids a whole class of surprising diffs. Treating only the newline as a line boundary (and a carriage return as ordinary text) is also the simplest rule to test.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Preserve all line endings exactly as they appeared. Only a newline marks the end of a line; a carriage return is ordinary text that passes through untouched. |
| B | Convert every line ending in the output to a plain newline, normalizing CRLF and bare CR input. |
| C | Preserve the exact characters, but treat a bare carriage return as a line boundary too, so no redaction can span it. |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (≤5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
